title: Binary Search with an Executable Trace
purpose: Programming fixture for invariants, code display, execution trace, variable state, missing-target behavior, and deterministic sandbox verification.

learner.audience: Beginning programmers who understand arrays, comparison, and loops.

objectives.statement: Explain the candidate-interval invariant and why sorted order is required.
criteria: Keeps the target in the remaining interval
Does not claim binary search works on arbitrary unsorted input

objectives.statement: Trace low, mid, high, and the compared value until index 5 is found.
Handle missing targets and empty input without out-of-bounds access.
criteria: Returns not found when low exceeds high
Performs no access for an empty list

claims.statement: If the target exists, each update keeps it inside the inclusive interval [low, high].
The declared trace finds target 23 at zero-based index 5 after midpoint values 16, 56, and 23.
Iterative binary search runs in O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

scenes.title: The sorted-data promise
scenes.narration: Binary search can discard a side only because the values are sorted. The candidate interval keeps every possible target position.
scenes.visualIntent: An ordered array and a bracketed inclusive interval; arrows and labels, not color alone, mark discarded positions.
scenes.captionText: Invariant: if target exists, it remains in [low, high].
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A sorted ten-item array has low and high brackets around all remaining candidates.

scenes.title: Safe midpoint and updates
scenes.narration: Compute mid from the current interval, compare once, then remove mid from the next interval. Stop when low is greater than high.
scenes.visualIntent: Syntax-highlighted inert pseudocode with a line-by-line reading order and no executable HTML.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: Pseudocode is available as text and highlights the current line without relying on color.

scenes.title: Find 23
scenes.narration: Compare 16 at index 4, then 56 at index 7, then 23 at index 5. Return 5.
scenes.visualIntent: A deterministic variable table and array pointer advance through exactly three steps.
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A three-row table lists low, mid, high, compared value, and update for every step.

scenes.title: Found, missing, and empty
scenes.narration: A missing target eventually leaves an empty interval. Empty input starts empty and never accesses an element. Each comparison halves the candidates.
scenes.visualIntent: Three labeled cases show result, not-found termination, and zero array accesses.
scenes.captionText: Stop when low > high • O(log n) time • O(1) space
scenes.accessibilityDescription: A comparison table describes found, absent, and empty-input outcomes.

qualityAssertions.description: Sandbox and authored trace agree on all low/mid/high states and result index.
Empty input executes no element access and returns not found.
Every factual claim has exact local support.
Highlighted code is also exposed in a deterministic textual reading order.
Trace visuals reflow rather than crop on portrait output.

provenance.notes: Algorithm, trace, and edge cases are locally authored and verified by exact assertions.
